title: Work Zone Safety for Vehicle Operators: Prevent Backing Incidents
summary: About five workers are killed each month and many more are injured when hit or backed over by a construction vehicle. Check the vehicle, avoid backing, and use a spotter and your back-up alarm.
talking_points: A delivery driver backed a truck without knowing two workers were still behind it. One worker jumped clear. The other, who had gone to check the tailgate, was hit and died.
Before you operate a vehicle, check the service, emergency, and parking brakes, back-up alarm or horn, steering, operating controls, tires, and seat belts.
Avoid backing up whenever possible. Park so you can pull in and out driving forward.
Keep mirrors clean and positioned correctly. Check blind spots and the area around you before you move.
Use a spotter and make sure you both understand the backing hand signals. Follow spotter and flagger directions. Stop if you lose sight of the spotter.
Use the back-up alarm or beep your horn two times before you reverse.
Do not back up more than 100 feet before you stop and check that the area is still clear.
Obey signs and follow the designated travel routes. Turn off the radio and put away distractions.
Keep your windows open so you can see and hear workers nearby, and wear your seat belt.
site_hazards_to_check: Back-up alarms, mirrors, brakes, or seat belts that do not work
Workers on foot behind or beside trucks, such as at tailgates
Tight or congested areas where backing is required
No spotter, flagger, or marked routes for vehicles
discussion_questions: What caused this incident, and how could it have been prevented?
Have you ever come close to hitting a worker? What happened?
What will we do at this worksite to avoid backing over or hitting workers?
